question: Under small random initialization, which parameter groups move first in a Transformer, when do query-key dynamics activate, and what conditions make directional condensation and normalized rank collapse mathematically inevitable?

key_findings.claim: Author theorem: the leading-order small-initialization gradient-flow system almost surely escapes its perturbative regime by finite-time blow-up.
key_findings.evidence: After expanding a one-layer tanh Transformer's exponential-loss objective in the initialization scale, the leading dynamics update the value and feed-forward parameters while query and key matrices are absent at leading order. Theorem 1 uses conservation laws, a Riccati-type energy inequality, and a measure-zero exclusion of degenerate Gaussian initializations to show the effective energy diverges in finite rescaled time. This is a statement about the truncated gradient-flow system, not literal finite-time divergence of the full AdamW-trained network.

key_findings.claim: Author theorem: value-matrix condensation follows only after imposing a strong sign-and-alignment condition on interacting rows and columns.
key_findings.evidence: Assumption 1 requires all relevant triple products to have positive alignment and every pair of induced row/column vectors to have positive inner product. Conditional on that state, Theorem 2 proves that rows of the value matrix align with one direction as the effective system approaches blow-up. The experiments show the measured satisfaction ratios approaching one, but the theory does not prove generic trajectories enter Assumption 1.

key_findings.claim: Author theorem: after an assumed dynamics-separation stage, query and key matrices obey a coupled linear ODE whose normalized limits collapse to rank one when its coupling matrix has a unique top singular value.
key_findings.evidence: Assumption 2 freezes outer parameters near a critical configuration and keeps query/key weights at order delta. Proposition 3 then derives dWQ/dt = F WK and dWK/dt = F-transpose WQ, with outer gradients one order smaller. Theorem 3 solves this linear system spectrally: a unique largest singular value makes the growing normalized component rank one. Degenerate top singular values permit higher-rank limits, and the result is conditional on the quasi-stationarity approximation.

anchors.section: Appendix A.3, Taylor expansion for the second stage

key_findings.claim: Author-reported experiment: a one-layer synthetic Transformer exhibits an outer-parameter phase, a loss plateau with attention takeover, and then query-key effective-rank reduction.
key_findings.evidence: On an anchor-function next-token task, the authors track parameter cosine matrices, relative norm changes, loss, and effective rank. Outer value/MLP weights change and condense first while query/key weights remain near initialization; during a plateau the relative update ordering reverses and attention ranks fall. Assumption-1 satisfaction ratios reportedly approach one within 200 steps, adjacent-time outer singular-vector similarity stays near one, and outer-versus-attention norms separate. These are trajectory diagnostics from a single described configuration, not a causal ablation establishing that condensation is required for performance.

anchors.section: Appendix B.1, synthetic setting and diagnostics

key_findings.claim: Author-reported scope extension: a small two-layer WikiText model shows qualitatively similar ordering of parameter-direction changes.
key_findings.evidence: The real-data run uses sequence length 2,048, model dimension 64, one head, two layers, residual connections, GeLU, no layer normalization, five epochs, and final-token-only loss. Figure 3 is reported to show outer matrices reorganizing before attention matrices. The paper provides no downstream metric, uncertainty across seeds, matched-initialization control, or numerical phase boundary, so this supports phenomenon recurrence in one modest language-modeling setup rather than architectural or scale universality.

key_findings.claim: Reviewer inference: the paper studies weight-matrix rank collapse after training begins, which is distinct from depth-wise token-representation collapse at initialization.
key_findings.evidence: Definitions 1-2 concern normalized parameter matrices, and Theorem 3 concerns WQ and WK under time evolution. Several neighboring papers instead analyze token representations becoming collinear as depth increases and the resulting gradient failure. Conflating those objects would overstate direct comparability: one can observe low-rank learned parameters without proving token collapse, and vice versa.

method.core_idea: Separate Transformer gradient flow by initialization scale: analyze an outer value/MLP subsystem first, then linearize query-key dynamics after the outer subsystem becomes quasi-stationary.
method.mechanism: A Taylor expansion around small Gaussian initialization yields a trilinear effective energy for value and feed-forward weights. Conservation and energy-growth arguments characterize escape and conditional condensation. A later expansion freezes those outer matrices and reduces query-key learning to a coupled linear system controlled by a data-dependent matrix F, whose top singular space determines normalized rank collapse.
assumptions: A one-layer, one-head Transformer with tanh, no residual connection or layer normalization, binary classification, exponential loss, continuous-time gradient flow, and sufficiently small Gaussian initialization for the main theory.
Assumption 1's global positivity/alignment conditions hold at some time before the effective system's singularity.
After first-stage breakdown, outer parameters are quasi-stationary and query/key matrices remain order delta as specified by Assumption 2 or its empirical proxy 2*.
The second-stage coupling matrix F has a unique largest singular value for rank-one rather than higher-rank collapse.
Higher-order Taylor terms can be neglected within each stated regime and empirical AdamW trajectories are informative proxies for gradient flow.

techniques.role: Control symmetry and rule out generic degenerate escape trajectories.
Show blow-up of the reduced outer-parameter system.
Characterize row-wise alignment separately from spectral rank.
Reduce late query-key dynamics to top-singular-mode amplification.
Track cosine structure, norm changes, singular-vector stability, and effective rank during training.

evaluations.setting: One-layer, one-head anchor-function synthetic next-token task with dimension 640 and AdamW
evaluations.metric: Loss phase, relative parameter-norm change, cosine-similarity structure, effective rank, and assumption-satisfaction ratios
evaluations.result: Qualitative three-stage trajectory; Assumption-1 satisfaction ratios approach one within the first 200 steps, outer directions stabilize, then query/key effective ranks fall during the plateau.
evaluations.baseline: Temporal comparison between outer value/MLP parameters and query/key parameters; no matched alternative-initialization or architecture baseline is reported.

evaluations.setting: Synthetic architecture with final activation removed
evaluations.metric: Same phase, cosine, norm, and effective-rank diagnostics
evaluations.result: Appendix figures show qualitatively similar dynamics, supporting the paper's omission of the final activation in second-stage analysis.

evaluations.setting: Two-layer, one-head WikiText final-token language modeling, dimension 64, sequence length 2,048, residuals and GeLU but no LayerNorm
evaluations.metric: Cosine-similarity evolution of parameter groups and training-loss phase
evaluations.result: Figure 3 reports outer-parameter reorganization preceding query/key reorganization in both layers.
evaluations.baseline: Qualitative correspondence with the synthetic trajectory; no standard LM-performance baseline or seed distribution.

limitations: Author-acknowledged: the principal theory is limited to binary classification because multi-class and sequence-to-sequence gradient-flow interactions are technically unresolved.
Reviewer-identified: condensation is conditional on Assumption 1; experiments suggest entry into the condition but the proof does not establish it from generic initialization.
Reviewer-identified: the second stage assumes the very quasi-stationarity and scale separation used to derive its linear query-key system.
Reviewer-identified: theoretical blow-up belongs to a truncated small-initialization gradient-flow approximation and should not be read as physical divergence of practical AdamW training.
Reviewer-identified: the WikiText model is tiny, single-head, lacks LayerNorm, uses only final-token loss, and has no reported perplexity, downstream quality, multi-seed variance, or scale sweep.
Reviewer-identified: experiments visualize correlation in one trajectory but do not intervene on condensation or rank to establish their causal contribution to optimization or generalization.
Reviewer-identified: weight-matrix rank collapse is not the same object as token-representation rank collapse, despite overlapping terminology in the field.
failure_modes: If sign/alignment conditions fail, the condensation theorem gives no conclusion even though outer parameters may still grow.
Tied leading singular values of F yield a multi-dimensional dominant subspace rather than guaranteed rank-one query/key limits.
Residuals, normalization, multi-head interactions, non-small initialization, discrete optimizers, and higher-order terms can destroy the clean scale separation.
A plateau plus rank reduction can be a symptom of representational degeneration rather than useful task specialization; the reported diagnostics alone do not distinguish the two.
Effective-rank and cosine plots without numerical thresholds or repeated runs permit ambiguous phase-boundary selection.
reusable_insights: Analyze parameter groups at the first nonzero order in initialization scale; delayed modules can become dominant only after earlier modules approach a stationary manifold.
Keep directional condensation, matrix spectral collapse, and token-representation collapse as distinct observables in mechanistic studies.
For staged-learning claims, measure relative update norms, subspace stability, loss derivatives, and effective rank together instead of inferring stages from loss alone.
A coupled bilinear ODE can turn a learned data-dependent matrix's singular spectrum into a precise prediction for which parameter directions dominate.
Empirical checks of a theorem's assumptions are valuable, but intervention and out-of-regime controls are needed before treating the assumed mechanism as causal.
open_questions: Can generic small-initialization trajectories be proved to enter Assumption 1, or can a measurable set avoid condensation?
Does the two-stage ordering persist across depth, heads, normalization variants, causal masking, realistic initialization, and optimizer state at modern language-model scale?
Does preventing query-key rank collapse improve or harm task loss, data efficiency, robustness, and compositional generalization?
Can F's spectrum be estimated early enough to prospectively predict final attention geometry rather than fit a post-hoc narrative?
What replaces the linear query-key ODE when several heads interact or when outer weights continue drifting on a comparable time scale?
How do parameter-rank dynamics relate quantitatively to hidden-state rank, gradient transport, and the loss-plateau phenomena documented in adjacent work?

competitive_landscape.title: Training Dynamics of Transformers to Recognize Word Co-occurrence via Gradient Flow Analysis
competitive_landscape.difference: Yang et al. also prove a two-phase shallow-Transformer gradient-flow trajectory in which an MLP aligns before attention, but for a concrete co-occurrence task and jointly trained softmax matrices from random initialization. Chen and Luo instead use a task-agnostic small-initialization expansion and target conditional parameter condensation plus query-key spectral collapse.

competitive_landscape.title: Scan and Snap: Understanding Training Dynamics and Token Composition in 1-layer Transformer
competitive_landscape.difference: Tian et al. derive an explicit attention scanning-and-phase-transition mechanism for next-token prediction under a faster decoder assumption. The present paper studies a different scale-separated trajectory induced by small initialization and expresses the late attention geometry through the singular modes of F.

competitive_landscape.title: Signal Propagation in Transformers: Theoretical Perspectives and the Role of Rank Collapse
competitive_landscape.difference: Noci et al. analyze token-representation collapse across depth at initialization and its vanishing-query/key-gradient consequences, proposing residual scaling. Chen and Luo analyze trained parameter matrices across time; their rank-collapse theorem concerns normalized WQ/WK rather than token states and is not inherently a training pathology.

competitive_landscape.title: What Happens During the Loss Plateau? Understanding Abrupt Learning in Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Gopalani and Hu connect algorithmic-task plateaus to hidden attention progress, repetition bias, and hidden-state representation collapse, including observations in Pythia and OLMo. The present paper offers a parameter-space gradient-flow explanation of a plateau-stage handoff but does not measure repetition bias or intervene on attention at comparable scale.

competitive_landscape.title: A Mechanistic Diagnostic of Rank Collapse in Post-Norm Decoder Transformers
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. study modern deep Post-Norm causal decoders and separate initialization-time token-similarity amplification from training-time backward repair failure, with 48-layer C4 experiments. That subsequent work targets hidden-state collapse as a harmful regime, whereas Chen and Luo predict late low-rank query/key parameters in small simplified models without establishing harm.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The work gives a task-light two-stage theory in which generic small-initialization outer dynamics blow up, conditional value-matrix condensation follows, and a later query-key system collapses spectrally, with synthetic and WikiText observations.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Theorems 1-3 cover the reduced first-stage escape, Assumption-1-conditional condensation, and Assumption-2-conditional normalized query-key limit. Figures 1-3 and appendix diagnostics show corresponding ordering in two experimental setups.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The strongest novelty is the explicit bridge from an initialization-scale expansion to two different geometric limits in value/MLP and query-key weights, plus the singular-spectrum formula for the second stage. Two-phase Transformer learning, attention plateaus, condensation, and rank collapse all predate it separately. Its generality is constrained by unproved stage-entry assumptions and limited empirical controls, while later deep-decoder work shows that the same terminology can describe a distinct, harmful hidden-state phenomenon.

reviewer_notes: Primary full text reviewed across all 29 extracted pages, including theorem proofs, experiment details, references, and compute disclosure. Competitive sources were checked on official NeurIPS or arXiv pages on 2026-08-23. Claims deliberately distinguish the full network from its reduced ODE and parameter rank from representation rank.
